Read this first

How a campaign works

A campaign is anything the pantry sells on the website: rubber ducks for the Duck Drop, tickets for a dinner, raffle-style items. Visitors choose how many they want, enter their details, pay by card on a secure Stripe page, and get a confirmation email. Every sale lands in a Google Sheet for the team.

Two kinds of campaign

TypeUse it forWhat is special
NumberedDuck Drop and anything else where each item needs its own numberEvery duck gets the next number (1, 2, 3 … or from a start number you choose). Buyers see their numbers right away and in their email. The sheet has one row per duck.
TicketsDinners, galas, eventsA "family ticket" can count as 4 people toward the event's capacity. The sheet has one row per order, with the number of people.

The four building blocks in Contentful

You build a campaign from four kinds of entries. Each one points to the next:

Pageshows aCampaign Sectionwhich uses aCampaignwhich sellsCampaign Items
EntryWhat it holdsExample
Campaign ItemOne thing for sale and its priceDuck, $10 · Family ticket, $100
CampaignThe sale itself: dates, limits, spreadsheet, the buyer's emailDuck Drop 2027
Campaign SectionThe form on a page, with a title and intro text"Adopt a Duck!"
PageThe web address where the form appears/duck-drop

Before you start, have these ready

  • What you are selling and the price of each item.
  • When sales open and close (optional).
  • Any limits: total available, per order, places held back for sponsors.
  • The text for the confirmation email and the thank-you message.
  • About 30 minutes, and access to Contentful and the pantry's Google Drive.
Important

Three rules that protect your sales data

  1. Never change a campaign's Campaign ID after the first sale. The website counts sales and hands out duck numbers by that ID.
  2. In the sales spreadsheet, never rename the first tab (Sheet1) and never move or delete the generated columns. You may add your own columns to the right.
  3. Always test a new campaign on a hidden page before you link to it (chapter 6).

Google Drive · 5 minutes

Create the sales spreadsheet

Every sale is written to a Google Sheet that belongs to the campaign. Create it first, because the campaign needs its ID.

  1. 1

    Create a new spreadsheet

    In Google Drive, open the pantry's shared folder for events (not your personal My Drive, so the sheet stays with the pantry). Click New → Google Sheets → Blank spreadsheet.

  2. 2

    Name it

    Click Untitled spreadsheet at the top left and type a clear name, for example Duck Drop 2027 – Online Sales.

    Leave the sheet empty and leave the tab at the bottom named Sheet1. The website writes the column headings itself when the first sale comes in.

  3. 3

    Share it with the website

    Click Share (top right). In "Add people", paste this address and choose Editor:

    donation-sheet-writer@pantry-shoppers.iam.gserviceaccount.com

    Untick Notify people (it is not a real inbox) and click Share. This is the website's own account; without it, sales cannot be written to the sheet.

  4. 4

    Keep it private

    In the same Share window, under General access, make sure it says Restricted. Add the team members who need to see sales. The sheet holds buyers' names, emails and phone numbers.

  5. 5

    Copy the spreadsheet ID

    Look at the address bar. The ID is the long code between /d/ and /edit:

    docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XVzgxftbQojfFFfDUR1-ktRVLMTQwrWqg4CPFpfslMc/edit

    Copy just that part. You will paste it into the campaign in chapter 4.

Tip

No sheet yet? You can leave the spreadsheet field empty and add it later. Sales are always stored safely, but only sales made after you add the ID appear in the sheet. Add it before you open sales.

Contentful · 5 minutes per item

Create the items for sale

Make one Campaign Item for each thing a buyer can choose: "Duck", "5-pack of ducks", "Adult ticket", "Family ticket". Items can be reused next year.

  1. 1

    Start a new entry

    In Contentful, open the Content tab and click Add entry.

  2. 2

    Choose "Campaign Item"

    Type Campaign in the search box at the top of the menu to shorten the list, then click Campaign Item.

  3. 3

    Name

    Type the name buyers will see, for example Duck or Adult ticket. It also appears on the payment page and in the sheet.

    Description (optional) is a short line under the name, such as "Dinner and dessert included" or "Admits 2 adults and 2 children".

  4. 4

    Price

    Enter the price in dollars, numbers only: 10, 40, 12.50.

  5. 5

    Units per item (only for packs and family tickets)

    How many ducks or people this item counts as. Leave empty for a normal item (it counts as 1).

    ItemUnits per ItemResult
    Duck(empty)1 duck, 1 number
    5-pack of ducks55 ducks with 5 consecutive numbers
    Family ticket4Counts as 4 people toward the event's capacity
  6. 6

    Limits (optional)

    Max per Order: the most of this item one buyer can take, for example 10 tickets. Total Available: stock for this item alone, for example 8 sponsor tables. Leave both empty for no limit.

  7. 7

    Fair market value (tickets with a meal or gift)

    If the buyer receives something of value, like dinner, enter its value per ticket here, for example 25 for a $40 dinner ticket. The confirmation email then includes the statement the IRS requires about how much of the payment is tax-deductible.

    Leave it empty for the Duck Drop.

  8. 8

    Publish

    Click the green Publish button on the right. Once an entry is published, that button reads Change status; after you edit a published entry it offers Publish changes, and your edits only reach the website after you click it. Repeat for each item.

Tip

Not sure about the fair market value? Ask the treasurer. A common approach is the cost per person of the meal the venue charges.

Contentful · 15 minutes

Create the campaign

The Campaign entry ties everything together: the items, the dates, the limits, the spreadsheet and the email buyers receive. Only the first few fields are required.

  1. 1

    Start a new Campaign

    Content → Add entry → Campaign.

  2. 2

    Name

    The name buyers see on the payment page and in their email, for example Duck Drop 2027 or Spring Gala 2027.

  3. 3

    Campaign ID

    A short code, lowercase with dashes, for example duck-drop-2027. It must be different from every earlier campaign, so include the year.

    Important

    Never change the Campaign ID once sales have started. The website keeps count of sales and duck numbers under this ID; a new ID starts from zero.

  4. 4

    Campaign Type

    Choose Numbered for the Duck Drop or Tickets for an event.

  5. 5

    Start Number (Numbered only)

    The number the first duck gets. Leave empty to start at 1. Use it when ducks are also sold on paper: if the paper forms use 1–500, enter 501 here.

    If you raise it later, the next duck jumps to the new number. Lowering it has no effect, so a number is never given out twice.

  6. 6

    Items

    Click Add content → Add existing content and pick the items you made in chapter 3. The order here is the order on the website; drag to rearrange.

  7. 7

    Open and close dates (optional)

    Open Date: sales start at this moment. Close Date: sales stop and visitors see the Closed Message instead of the form. Leave both empty to sell straight away with no end date.

    Tip

    Check the time zone next to each time. It should show Eastern time: UTC-04:00 in summer, UTC-05:00 in winter. Choose it from the list if it shows something else.

  8. 8

    Limits (optional)

    Total Capacity: how many ducks or people in total. For tickets this counts people, so a family ticket uses 4.

    Reserved Spots: places held back from the total for sponsors, volunteers or VIPs who don't buy online. You can change this at any time.

    Max Items per Order: the most items one buyer can take in one order.

    Leave any of these empty for no limit. Example: a hall for 120 with 10 seats for sponsors → Total Capacity 120, Reserved Spots 10, so 110 are sold online.

  9. 9

    Offer to cover fees

    Turn on to show the checkbox "Help cover the credit card processing fee". Most buyers leave it ticked, so the pantry receives the full price. Cover Fees Label changes its wording.

  10. 10

    Spreadsheet ID

    Paste the ID you copied in chapter 2. Paste only the ID, not the whole link; Contentful will warn you if you paste a link.

  11. 11

    The confirmation email

    Every buyer gets this email right after paying. Write it in the Confirmation Email Subject and Confirmation Email Body fields. Words in curly brackets are filled in for each buyer:

    WriteBecomesExample
    {firstName}Buyer's first nameJane
    {lastName}Buyer's last nameExample
    {campaignName}The campaign's NameDuck Drop 2027
    {count}How many ducks or places2
    {numbers}Their duck numbers101, 102
    {total}Amount paid$20.91
    {orderId}Order numberHPS-MVZLG280-1A2B
    {orderSummary}A small table of what they bought, with the total. Put it on a line by itself.(table)

    Use **double asterisks** for bold and a blank line between paragraphs. If you leave the body empty, a short standard email is sent. For a Numbered campaign the duck numbers are always included, even if you forget {numbers}.

    This is what the buyer receives:

  12. 12

    Sender and replies (optional)

    Confirmation Email From: leave empty to send from website@hollistonpantryshelf.org. A different sender, such as ducks@, must first be set up by the website administrator.

    Confirmation Email Reply-To: where buyers' replies go, for example the event coordinator's address.

  13. 13

    Messages on the website

    Success Headline and Success Body: the thank-you page after payment.
    Closed Message: shown instead of the form outside the open and close dates.
    Sold Out Message: shown when everything is sold.

  14. 14

    Publish

    Click Publish. The campaign is ready but not yet visible anywhere; that is the next chapter.

Contentful · 5 minutes

Put it on the website

A campaign appears on the website through a Campaign Section on a Page. You can give it a page of its own (best for the Duck Drop) or add it to an existing page.

A. Create the section

  1. 1

    Add a Campaign Section

    Content → Add entry → Campaign Section. Enter a Title (the heading on the page, such as "Adopt a Duck!") and an Intro Text explaining the event, the date and what buyers get.

  2. 2

    Link the campaign

    Under Campaign, click Add content → Add existing content and choose your campaign. Pick a Background Style if you like, then Publish.

B1. On a new page

  1. 3

    Create the page

    Content → Add entry → Page. Fill in an Internal Title and a Slug: the web address, starting with a slash, such as /duck-drop.

  2. 4

    Add the section

    Under Sections, click Add content → Add existing content, choose the Campaign Section, then Publish. The page is now live at that address, but nobody can find it yet. Test it now (chapter 6) before you link to it.

  3. 5

    Link to it from the menu (after testing)

    Open the Navigation Menu entry, add a Button / Link under Menu Items with the text and the slug, and publish. Or link to the page from a button on the homepage or in the announcement bar.

B2. Or on an existing page

  1. 3

    Add the section to the page

    Open the page, for example Support. Under Sections, click Add content → Add existing content, choose the Campaign Section, drag it into place and Publish. It is visible to everyone immediately, so do this after testing.

Before you announce it

Test it like a buyer

Open the page and walk through it exactly as a buyer would. This is also what you will see when you help someone over the phone.

  1. 1

    Choose quantities

    Use + and −, or type a number. The buttons stop at any limit you set.

  2. 2

    Enter details

    First and last name, email, and phone are all required. The phone number must be a US number; it is tidied up automatically, e.g. (508) 555-0123.

  3. 3

    Check the fee and total

    The fee checkbox is ticked by default. The total updates as you go.

  4. 4

    Continue to payment

    The buyer goes to Stripe's secure payment page. The items are reserved for them for 30 minutes while they pay.

  5. 5

    Pay on Stripe

    Stripe shows the pantry's name, each item and the total. Stripe sometimes offers its quick-pay service "Link" first; buyers can click Pay without Link to pay normally by card.

  6. 6

    Changed their mind?

    The back arrow at the top left returns to the form and releases the reserved items straight away.

  7. 7

    Thank-you page

    After paying, the buyer returns to the same page and sees your thank-you message, their order number, and for the Duck Drop their duck numbers.

  8. 8

    Confirmation email

    Within a minute the email from chapter 4 arrives (check the spam folder the first time). The sale also appears in the spreadsheet.

Important

Do one real test purchase of the cheapest item before you announce the campaign, then refund it in Stripe (chapter 8). It is the only way to be sure the payment, the email and the sheet all work. The refund costs the pantry Stripe's small fee, about 60 cents.

A ticket campaign looks like this

While sales are open

View sales and make changes

See who bought what

Open the campaign's spreadsheet. A new row appears within a minute of each payment. Sort or filter it like any sheet. Don't move or delete the generated columns; add your own to the right, such as "Checked in" or "Prize".

Duck Drop: one row per duck. Column C is the duck number, so on the day you can look up any number instantly.

Tickets: one row per order. The People column (H) counts family tickets as 4.

To find outIn the sheet
Ducks sold so farThe highest number in column C, or =COUNTA(C2:C)
People coming (tickets)=SUM(H2:H)
Money raisedUse Stripe's dashboard (it shows refunds too), or add up each order once
Someone's orderSearch the sheet (Ctrl/⌘ F) for their name or email

How much is left

When an item has a limit, the website shows Only N left once 20 or fewer remain, and Sold out at zero. When everything is gone, the Sold Out Message replaces the form.

Common changes

You want to…Do this in the campaign (then Publish)
Hold back more places for sponsorsRaise Reserved Spots. Lower it to release them for sale.
Sell more than plannedRaise Total Capacity (or the item's Total Available).
Stop sales nowSet Close Date to now. Visitors see the Closed Message.
Extend salesMove the Close Date later.
Change the email or messagesEdit them. New buyers get the new text straight away.
Change a priceEdit the item's Price. Only new orders pay the new price.
Add an item (e.g. a 10-pack)Create the Campaign Item and add it to Items.
Tip

Changes in Contentful reach the website within about a minute. Refresh the page to see them.

Helping buyers

Refunds and buyer questions

Refunds are done in Stripe by someone with access to the pantry's Stripe account (usually the treasurer).

  1. 1

    Find the payment

    Go to dashboard.stripe.com → Payments and search for the buyer's email address. The payment description includes the campaign name and order number, such as Duck Drop 2027 — HPS-MVZLG280-1A2B.

  2. 2

    Refund it

    Open the payment, click Refund, choose the full amount or part of it, pick a reason and confirm. The buyer gets the money back in 5–10 days. Stripe keeps its small processing fee.

  3. 3

    Mark it in the sheet

    Add a column on the right called Refunded and mark the buyer's row(s). Don't delete the rows: they are your record of what happened.

  4. 4

    Give the places back (only if the campaign has a limit)

    The website still counts a refunded order as sold. To put the places back on sale, lower Reserved Spots by that many (a family ticket = 4). If Reserved Spots is already 0, raise Total Capacity instead. Refunded duck numbers are not reused.

Questions you may get

Buyer says…What to do
"I didn't get my email."Find them in the sheet. If the row is there, the payment worked: ask them to check spam, and send their order number and duck numbers from your own email. If there is no row, check Stripe; if Stripe shows no payment, they did not complete checkout.
"I made a typo in my name or email."Correct it in the sheet. Nothing else needs to change.
"Can I swap my duck numbers?"No. Numbers are given in order of purchase and can't be changed.
"It says sold out but I need tickets."If you have Reserved Spots left, sell them directly and lower Reserved Spots, or release some for online sale.
"The form won't accept my phone number."It must be a US number with area code, e.g. 508 555 0123.

When it is over

Close the campaign

  1. 1

    Stop sales

    Set the Close Date (if you didn't already) and publish. The Closed Message shows from then on.

  2. 2

    Remove the links

    After the event, remove the menu link and any buttons pointing to the page. Then either unpublish the page or remove the section from it.

  3. 3

    Keep the records

    Don't delete the Campaign entry or the spreadsheet; they are the record of the event. Move the sheet into an archive folder if you like.

  4. 4

    Next year

    Make a new Campaign with a new Campaign ID (duck-drop-2028) and a new spreadsheet. You can reuse the items. Never reuse an old Campaign ID: it would continue last year's numbering and counts.

Troubleshooting

If something looks wrong

What you seeLikely cause and fix
The page shows the title but no formThe campaign or its items are not published, or no item has a price. Publish them all.
"Sales are currently closed" before the startThe Open Date is in the future or the Close Date has passed. Check both, including the time and AM/PM.
"This campaign could not be found"The campaign is unpublished, or its Campaign ID was changed. Change it back and publish.
A buyer paid but the sheet has no rowThe sheet ID is missing or wrong, the sheet is not shared with the website as Editor, or the first tab was renamed. Fix it and tell the website administrator: earlier sales can be recovered.
Columns in the sheet are shiftedSomeone inserted or moved a column. Move it back; new rows always follow the original order.
No confirmation emailsCheck the website@ mailbox's Sent folder, then contact the website administrator.
Changes in Contentful don't showDid you click Publish? Wait a minute and refresh.

For anything else, contact the website administrator with the campaign name, the buyer's email and the time of purchase.

Questions about this guide or the website? Ask the website administrator.
